This course introduction explains the origins and
complexities of the modern Middle East, focusing on
the arbitrary creation of states by colonial powers and
their lasting impact.
Creation of Middle Eastern States
- Middle Eastern states were established by Britain
and France after World War I through colonial officials
drawing borders arbitrarily.
- These states differ from European nation-states,
which are generally more homogeneous and based
on shared language and culture.
Consequences of Arbitrary Borders
- The artificial nature of these states has contributed
to ongoing destabilization, disorder, and chaos in the
region.
